background_notes.fact: The affine map i0:X→Z, i0(y)=(y,t0), is C∞ with Fréchet derivative h↦(h,0). For every x∈X, the curves h↦x+h v0 and h↦(x+h v0,t0) have derivatives v0 and (v0,0)=σ(j0), respectively, at 0.

background_notes.justification: For an affine map a+L(y), subtracting its value and L applied to the increment leaves zero remainder. Here the displayed linear parts are bounded; their derivatives are constant and all derivatives of order at least two vanish. The same zero-remainder calculation gives the two ordinary curve derivatives.

background_notes.justification: The time projection is continuous, so Ω is open; at (x,t0) a sufficiently small neighborhood has positive time. C∞ regularity includes first Fréchet differentiability on this neighborhood. A within-domain derivative at an interior point is an ordinary derivative because all sufficiently small increments remain in the domain. Values of the representatives outside Ω do not enter this local limit.

background_notes.justification: An ordinary derivative is the limit in the normed space V of the difference quotient as nonzero h tends to zero. Such a limit is unique: if two candidate limits differ, the triangle inequality and convergence force the norm of their difference to be zero. Applying this to each pair of identical curves gives exactly the two displayed equalities, with Ddir interpreted by D008.
